summary.text: 住 is analyzed as a phono-semantic character: 人 in its side form 亻 contributes the person category, and 主 supplies a sound cue. Its common meanings include “reside” and “stay”; reference works also describe “stop” or “remain” as an early or basic use.

formation.text: The supported reference analysis combines 人, written in the side form 亻, with 主 as a phonetic component. This analysis does not establish the character’s formation date or early graphic sequence.

components.text: 亻 is the positional side form of 人 and contributes the person category in 住.

主 is analyzed as the phonetic component. Baxter–Sagart’s Old Chinese forms are similar but distinct, making a sound relationship plausible without proving its precise history. The supplied image is a modern redraw of a seal-script-style 主, not an early form of 住.

sound.text: The Old Chinese forms are similar but distinct in this reconstruction system, supporting a possible phonetic relationship without establishing its exact history.
The Middle Chinese readings differ, so this pair does not itself show a close sound match; the Old Chinese pair in this same system is similar and supports the proposed relationship’s plausibility.
The supplied modern Mandarin readings are similar but distinct; this comparison alone does not demonstrate an ancient phonetic role.
sound.system: Modern Mandarin, supplied local Unihan readings

history.text: No dated early glyph sequence or graphic change is established for 住. One reference says the character is absent from Shuowen, but this does not show that it was absent from earlier scripts. The curated image depicts 主 in a modern redraw of a seal-script style, not an artifact or an early form of 住.

Old Chinese reconstructions differ by source: one gives *tos/*dos for 住 and *tjoʔ for 主, while Baxter–Sagart gives *dro(ʔ)-s and *toʔ. These are separate analyses; the Baxter–Sagart comparison makes a phonetic relationship plausible but does not prove the character’s sound history.

uncertainties.text: Reference works support the formation analysis, but the character’s formation date and early graphic sequence remain unresolved in the supplied evidence.

Reported early examples for “remain/stop” come from transmitted texts, whose dating does not securely establish the earliest attestation. The proposed semantic path describes word usage, not graphic evolution.
The original referent of 主 is unsettled. Its proposed role as a sound component in 住 does not depend on identifying that referent; the cited Old Chinese comparison supports plausibility, not proof.

Other listed uses include verbal-complement uses, “straight,” use with 駐, and a variant relation with 往. Their chronology and connections are unresolved; the evidence does not support treating 住 as a whole-character borrowing from 主.

senses.period: Western Han and later uses reported; secure earliest attestation unresolved
senses.text: A usage account reports a transmitted Western Han example for “stay/remain” and discusses early medical-text examples, while noting that transmission and dating do not settle the earliest attestation. Reference works also describe “stop/remain” as a basic or early sense.

senses.period: Late Han–Three Kingdoms texts reported; attested more widely later
senses.text: A usage study reports residence uses in late Han–Three Kingdoms texts and says they became dominant by the Eastern Jin. These are literary-text attestations, not securely dated manuscript evidence.
Dictionaries record lodging and staying among the uses of 住, but the evidence does not date this sense or establish its precise relation to “stop/remain” and “reside.”

developments.text: A usage account proposes development from stopping or remaining toward lodging and residence. The reported sequence concerns word use; its exact chronology is unresolved.

limitations.text: The proposed early examples are transmitted textual evidence, not securely dated manuscript attestations; the earliest use of each sense remains unresolved.
Dictionary lists include other uses, but undated glosses do not establish their order or semantic connections.

overview.text: 住 is analyzed with 亻 for the person category and 主 as a sound cue. It commonly means “reside” or “stay”; “stop/remain” is also described as an early or basic use.

components.text: 亻 is the side form of 人 and contributes the person category in 住.
主 supplies a sound cue. Similar Old Chinese forms make the relationship plausible, but do not prove its precise history.

relationships.text: In the reference analysis of 住, 亻 is the positional form of 人 and contributes the person category.

Reference works analyze 主 as the sound component. In Baxter–Sagart 2014, 主 *toʔ and 住 *dro(ʔ)-s are similar but distinct Old Chinese reconstructions, supporting a possible relationship without proving its precise phonetic history.
